links.outcome: Effect of locally adjusted DL thresholds on workload reduction and NPV in chest radiograph screening
links.effect: Threshold adjustment to 95% sensitivity ruled out about 40% of cases for single-disease screening with NPV around 99%; default Youden thresholds gave sensitivity 85.33%, specificity 75.1%.
links.quote: It might enable a significant workload reduction of about 40% in ruling out specific diseases, thereby maintaining sensitivities above 95% and NPVs around 99% when reasonable optimized cutoff values for DL results are applied.

links.outcome: Influence of sex, age, multimorbidity on DL-radiologist agreement
links.effect: In gold-standard negatives, multimorbidity (β=0.151), age (β=0.089) and sex (β=-0.038) significantly influenced DL results; in positives, female sex (β=0.153, p=0.026) linked to lower DL results.
links.quote: Significant effects were found for the parameters of multimorbidity ( β = 0.151, p < 0.001), age ( β = 0.089, p < 0.001), and sex ( β = −0.038, p = 0.031; sex was dummy coded using “0” for male and “1” for female).

links.outcome: Accuracy of combined comprehensive reading of seven abnormalities without human supervision
links.effect: Combined reading: sensitivity 31.37%, specificity 14.55%; 364 (76.31%) patients with false positives and 35 (7.34%) with missed findings; not suitable for unsupervised use.
links.quote: Therefore and as of today, DL applications appear not to be suitable for completely unsupervised application in the clinical setting.

links.outcome: Single-site performance dependence and generalizability of DL
links.effect: Monocentric study with one X-ray machine; authors recommend institution-specific cutoff validation; foreign material did not significantly affect results.
links.quote: In a next step, DL software such as presented in this study could be applied as a second layer, thereby generating specific diagnoses for the “abnormal” cases using tailor-made cutoff values, which at best can be validated by test data for every institution.

links.outcome: missed findings in standalone comprehensive reporting
links.effect: About 13% workload reduction, but missed findings in around 7.34% of patients.
links.quote: The findings for these cutoff values would allow for some workload reduction of about 13% but at the cost of missing findings in around 7.34% of patients, which is not acceptable, as the minimum goal of applying DL tools in the clinical setting should be noninferiority to the current gold standard to avert potential danger for patients.

links.effect: At ≥95% sensitivity cutoffs: 31 (6.5%) true positive, 197 (41.3%) true negative, 248 (51.99%) false positive, 1 (0.21%) false negative.
links.quote: When scanning for only one kind of abnormal finding using these cutoff values, on average around 31 (6.5%) of all cases were classfied true positive, 197 (41.3%) true negative, 248 (51.99%) false positive, and 1 (0.21%) case false negative.
